title: #499: How High Is Your Ceiling? Reality Fracture Drafts
scale: Letter grades (A+ to F), used sparingly; most cards discussed in terms of floor and ceiling rather than graded

cards.take: The blue enchantment-removal spell is very bad, and if you find yourself playing it something has gone wrong in your draft.
Admits he has put it in a few decks, but doesn't defend it as a card worth chasing.
Wasn't on his radar, but its strong data makes sense: it ramps, fills the graveyard, and has menace to pressure planeswalkers, so it's rising in his pick order.
Mediocre win rate hides a Wrenn and Six-style ceiling; it's nuts on an uncontested turn two, but you must protect it and surround it with loyalty synergies rather than sad-playing it and downticking.
Finally played it alongside Way of the Paradox and found it as good as advertised, happily scooping up copies others undervalue because of the data.
An Uro-like engine that, with Way of the Pyromancer and Inspired Tethermage, lets you dump lands and generate huge amounts of mana and loyalty.
Paired with Way of the Pyromancer in an actual deck, it lived up to the hype.
Best friends with the Way of enchantments because each loyalty uptick grows it, and its six-mana Jace activation gives a great mana sink in long games.
A classic high-toughness build-around for WU or WB defenders; it can often wheel, so note it and only commit if pieces like Tetsuko come.
Worth speculating on in low-power drafts, but its value swings from B+ to F depending on support, so don't chase support early.
Not quite never-pass but well above Ghalta; bouncing Way of enchantments, planeswalkers, or Plan for All Outcomes creates lock-like loops, though it needs early board presence.
An A+ when you hit its ceiling with ETB permanents like Fateshaper Aspirant, but a D/F without support; not giving yourself the chance to build around it leaves equity on the table.
An ideal Rescue Girl companion since you can bounce and replay it to keep recovering legendary cards in long games.
An incredible repeatable empower source in his Jeskai surveil deck that also removes threats and pairs with Rescue Girl and Way of the Pyromancer upticks.
Has the highest floor of the ceiling cards while still having a high ceiling; great in control and EJ-uptick decks, and a steal at pick seven.
Nuts if you can reliably cast it cheaply after another spell, like a two-drop with omit variables or Unsummon, and still fine at full four mana.
Very strong and worth pursuing aggressively, usually costing one to five mana in RG ramp or GW big-creature decks.
Explosive turn-one ramp in RG with plenty of mana sinks like Inspired Tethermage, but it needs top end such as Craftwork Crusher to ramp into.
Payoff for seed-suture and targeting decks that needs no mana investment, which he thinks makes it significantly better than Prof.
Only as good as your count of targeting spells like seed suture, and harder to turn on than Prof.
A late pick that's good only in a deck caring about repeatable life gain, and bad otherwise.
Free repeatable noncombat damage makes it good in red-black decks that care about it, but poor anywhere else.
A 2/1 flyer alone falls short, but with +1/+1-counter creatures it shines by lifting big monsters into the air.
Weak body for three mana, but one counter trigger pays it off and it's a great onboard trick in seed-suture decks, especially with Blossom-Blessed Angel.
Very good, especially when paired with Yoshimaru to grow into a large flyer.
Nuts when you have a Jace out, making a true draw-go control deck possible, and even as a Cancel it's fine because long games have critical spells to counter.
Previously dismissed as unplayable, but it creates infinite mana with Loot, the Nexus given four distinct powers and a mana sink.
Combines with Hapatra, the Desert Frost for infinite mana that can feed sinks like Inspired Tethermage or Wrecking Gecko.
Fine in WU scry decks and should come to you there, but not powerful enough to take early due to the two-mana tax.
Prefers it over Danitha because it's a good two-drop easily turned on by Empower Jace and peer-review cadets.
Very strong in Empower Jace decks that stay ahead, since copying a spell late is far better than drawing a card.
A mea culpa after early hype: it's unplayable and not worth chasing.
Can be good as a self-contained sacrifice outlet when you have disposable bodies like Rank Rat to curve into it.
Not a good card alone, but an outstanding 22nd-23rd card in lifegain or Way of the Paradox decks.
Seemed a nothing burger, but four copies as reliable 3/3 flyers powered his rareless 7-1 UB deck; still never a first pick.
Not worth a pick investment, but if RW is open you should expect to see it late and support it with seed sutures.
Slightly better than Prudent Fateseer in a weak pack because it has a higher ceiling.
Strong and more flexible than Way of the Healer; taking it first is perfectly defensible.
Pushes back that the 1/4 drain flyer is a good card.
Not impressed by it yet.
Barely affects games because life totals rarely matter.
Concedes it's mostly a sideboard card, only a 23rd-card filler for Abzan lifegain or Way of the Necromancer.
Premium removal that kills almost everything despite expectations about +1/+1 counters, clearly the best card in a weak pack.
Premium removal he took to pair with Multiply by Zero, but he'd take Way of the Pyromancer over it with an empty pool.
A really good splashable gold card with higher floor and ceiling than Generous Revival.
Almost a WB gold card that matches Recursive Recruitment in power when it has targets like Rescue Girl.
High on it as a safe mono-color pick that churns through his deck and triggers prowess in long games.
Would take Countersculpt over it since both are effectively double blue.
Excellent in his UB discard deck because it pings off discards from your own looting and cycling.
Clearly the best card in the pack and correct to take for its ceiling even as a gold card.
Would take it over most cards, but regrets passing it for Way of the Warlord while chasing the Kraken plan.
Not that good a card, and even its blue-white data is unremarkable.
A cool card that empowers Jace eight, his preferred way to make Krakens.
Regrets taking it over Hapatra, admitting he was too Kraken-focused.
A card he likes for reanimating creatures or planeswalkers while empowering Jace.
Never worth a pick but a good 23rd card that protects planeswalkers, enables Ghalta, and shuffles away threats like the blue Sphinx.
Took it in a weak pack because it has a real ceiling with small evasive creatures.
In a messy draft, take it to secure fixing, since you'll likely end up two colors plus a splash.
Better than Countersculpt in Empower Jace decks because it plays to the board and goes unblockable with Tetsuko.
Strong in his triple-Countersculpt deck when cast late, but tapping out for it on turn four is generally bad.
Doesn't love it and wouldn't take it early.
A good trick that's especially scary with large green creatures.

format.summary: Reality Fracture is near-GOAT tier: power is spread across all colors and pairs, so color rankings don't matter; the key is finding card ceilings by building around uncommons supported by the right commons, letting the open lane reveal itself, and drafting cards first then decks.
format.speed: Games last long but aren't slow; you must still play to the board early, with two-for-ones and grinding trades common, long games rewarding mana sinks, and constructed decks outlasting piles of good cards.

colors.take: Supports many builds like seed-suture counters, cadets, high-toughness Ghalta, and Rescue Girl ETBs.
Blue-white leads the early data; Countersculpt can enable real draw-go control and blue has strong Empower Jace and prowess tools.
Black commons and uncommons hold up: discard, cheap removal like Multiply by Zero, and grinding cards carried a rareless deck, though the black Way of enchantments disappointed.
Way of the Pyromancer offers a big ceiling in loyalty decks, while cards like Koth, the Geomancer need a noncombat-damage shell.
Green provides ramp, big bodies, and mana sinks, with Heartwood Crafter, Ghalta, and Inspired Tethermage among standouts.

pairs.take: Top of early data and flexible, with cadets, high-toughness Ghalta and Tetsuko, Rescue Girl, or Empower Jace control builds possible.
Ethan's rareless 7-1 deck won with discard, spot removal, and Theorix Metamage flyers; Recursive Recruitment is worth splashing.
The ramp deck: Heartwood Crafter, Inspired Tethermage, Way of the Paradox/Pyromancer, and top end like Craftwork Crusher and Ghalta.
Twisted Fates and Generous Revival are payoffs, and high-toughness Ghalta fits here too.
Expanding into Temur with Kiora and Plan for All Outcomes gives a strong loyalty-uptick engine.
Viable only if open, needing late Skilled Battlecarvers and seed sutures.
Seed-suture counters with Danitha, Yoshimaru, Tomik, and Blossom-Blessed Angel, plus big green bodies for Ghalta the Unstoppable.
Primal Witchstalker is putting up strong numbers, and Hapatra, the Desert Fang is a strong gold card.
Prowess and noncreature spells pair with Traxos, while Saheeli, Jewel of Avishkar is underwhelming.
Noncombat damage with Koth, the Geomancer and Tinybones; discard punishes greedy ramp decks.

mechanics.name: Empower Jace
mechanics.take: Central to the format: build to never fall behind, attack opponents' Jace tokens as a default, and remember that an ignored high-loyalty Jace runs away with games.

mechanics.name: Prepared spells (seed suture, peer review, omit variables)
mechanics.take: Seed suture powers counter payoffs, peer review cadets enable surveil, and omit variables triggers prowess cheaply.

mechanics.name: Way of enchantments
mechanics.take: High-ceiling, low-floor cards like Pyromancer, Paradox, Cryomancer, and Healer reward loyalty-centered builds that defend them, while black versions disappoint.

mechanics.name: Scry/Surveil
mechanics.take: Prof, Prudent Fateseer, and Saheeli, Consul of Oversight reward repeatable scry or surveil from Jace or cadets.

mechanics.name: Land cycling and fixing
mechanics.take: Land cyclers are good fillers for making land drops and late threats, and Room of Refuge enables three-color decks.

mechanics.name: Mana sinks
mechanics.take: Repeatable lands like Theorist's Sanctum or activations are valuable in long games.

advice: Don't soft-force colors; take the most powerful cards early and let the open lane emerge.
Gather about five strong cards, then high-ceiling uncommons, then commons supporting them.
In low-power drafts, keep speculating through picks four to seven to find an uncontested lane.
Avoid early commitment to build-arounds like Ghalta or Rescue Girl; let support come before investing.
Draft cards, then decks; build-arounds without support become dead cards.
Track which cards can wheel, like Ghalta the Immovable, to plan packages.
Treat win-rate data cautiously; it shows plug-and-play strength, not ceilings like Way of the Pyromancer.
Default to removing opponents' Jace tokens; ignoring them hands over value.
Expect long games and favor two-for-ones and mana sinks.
Prioritize removal, as many ceilings lie in on-board creatures and Jace tokens.
Use discard against ramp decks needing all their lands and top end.
